## Answer

**`mysql` — `SQL SELECT`** (the query issued by the `customer` service's `/customer` handler) accounts for the largest share of the extra time.

### How I got there
- Pulled all `/dispatch` root traces from `frontend` over the last 24h (51 traces, all from a load-test burst around 2026-08-09 19:29–19:30 UTC).
- Fastest: **669,553 µs** (`3f185804...`) — Slowest: **797,434 µs** (`2e5db112...`)
- Extra time in the slow trace: **127,881 µs**
- Ran `get_critical_path` on both and diffed self-time aggregated by (service, span name) along the critical path:

| Operation | Fast (µs) | Slow (µs) | Δ (µs) | Share of extra time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **mysql / SQL SELECT** | 285,311 | 360,512 | **+75,201** | **~59%** |
| redis-manual / GetDriver | 174,985 | 201,946 | +26,961 | ~21% |
| redis-manual / FindDriverIDs | 13,428 | 33,903 | +20,475 | ~16% |
| route / /route | 183,435 | 190,292 | +6,857 | ~5% |
| (driver, frontend self-time, customer) | — | — | net -1,613 | ~-1% |

The `mysql SQL SELECT` span (child of `customer`'s `/customer` span) alone grew from 285ms to 361ms, roughly 59% of the total 128ms slowdown — dwarfing the combined Redis (`GetDriver`/`FindDriverIDs` under `driver`'s `FindNearest`) and routing-service contributions.
